summary: IDP assertion timestamp (fractional seconds) rounding leads to 'Conditions not yet valid' and 401s in private VPC
description: Issue summary: Several of NorthStar Analytics' scheduled batch workers fail to exchange a SAML assertion for a service token when calling Redwood's token-exchange endpoint in their private VPC. The exchange returns a 401 with assertion validation errors referencing condition timestamps. Impact: A subset of nightly batch jobs (data enrich, nightly-feedback-indexer) are failing and falling back to slower pipelines; customer reports 30% job failure rate since 2026-03-09 23:00 UTC. Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) behind edge-proxy v1.12.2 and an on-prem IdP (SAML) which emits ISO-8601 timestamps with fractional seconds (e.g. 2026-03-10T23:01:45.123Z).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use the customer's SAML IdP to issue a signed assertion containing Conditions NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter timestamps with millisecond precision (example: 2026-03-10T23:01:45.123Z).
2) From a scheduled worker inside the private VPC, POST the assertion to /token-exchange (private control plane) with the usual x-tenant header.
3) Observe the token-exchange response: 401 with body 'Assertion conditions not yet valid' or 'Assertion expired'.
4) If you remove fractional seconds from the assertion timestamps (2026-03-10T23:01:45Z), the exchange succeeds.
5) Reproduce test by sending SAML assertion through customer's nginx ingress (with header rewrite) to observe rounding/truncation effects.
observed_behavior: Token exchange fails intermittently with 401. Logs on token-exchange: 'Assertion conditions not yet valid: NotBefore=2026-03-10T23:01:45.000Z vs current=2026-03-10T23:01:45.123Z' (timestamps appear swapped/rounded), and signature verification succeeds. Failures correlated with assertions passing through the customer's ingress + our idp-proxy.
expected_behavior: Token exchange should accept SAML Conditions that include fractional seconds (ISO-8601 with milliseconds) within standard time-skew allowances, or the proxy should preserve the original timestamp precision so validation uses the assertion's actual values.
logs: 2026-03-10T23:01:46.234Z token-exchange ERROR tenant=ns-42 assertion_id=abc123 AssertionValidation: ConditionsNotYetValid NotBefore=2026-03-10T23:01:45.000Z now=2026-03-10T23:01:45.123Z
2026-03-10T23:01:46.235Z token-exchange INFO tenant=ns-42 assertion_id=abc123 signature=OK issuer=urn:ids:example IdPSubject=svc-batch-worker
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: time skew between client and server. Ruled out: NTP on worker host within ±20ms, customer confirmed clock sync.

Observed that the forwarded header from customer's nginx sometimes has timestamps truncated to second precision. Replayed SAML through customer's ingress in staging and confirmed header rewrite rule uses a format string that drops fractional seconds (nginx config: $date_iso8601 yields no milliseconds in some builds).

Edge case: our idp-proxy expects canonical ISO-8601 and accepts fractional seconds; however when the assertion is forwarded via X-Assert-Timestamp header the truncated value is used for validation in some code paths. The proxy code path that reads header uses an internal parser that coerces to seconds and ends up comparing a rounded timestamp against the signed assertion, producing a NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter mismatch.
Reproduced locally by inserting a middleware in idp-proxy that force-truncates timestamp; token exchange fails with identical error.

Related code: idp-proxy/pkg/saml/conditions.go (parsing + header fallback) appears to fall back to header timestamp before falling back to assertion timestamp when header is present. A change in edge-proxy/nginx variable expansion upstream started dropping fractional seconds during a recent ingress upgrade at the customer.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reported batch workers started failing after they upgraded their on-prem ingress on 2026-03-09. Provided initial logs and reproduction steps.
Evan Morales (SRE) 2026-03-11: Confirmed reproduction in staging. Hypothesis: header rewrite truncates milliseconds. Reached out to ENG to evaluate idp-proxy parsing behavior.

Lina Gomez (Customer Infra - NorthStar) 2026-03-11: We upgraded nginx from 1.20.2 -> 1.24.1 and changed logging variable. We can revert or change config; curious if Redwood can accept truncated header as fallback.

Tomás Rivera (Eng - idp-proxy) 2026-03-12: Found code path where we prefer forwarded header over assertion timestamp. Preparing a patch to prefer assertion XML value and to accept fractional seconds in header parsing. Draft PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1427
Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-12: Customer applied temporary workaround: adjusted nginx rewrite to preserve fractional seconds. Batch failures dropped to zero in their next run.
root_cause: Ingress header rewrite at customer side truncated fractional seconds combined with idp-proxy code path that prioritized the forwarded header over the assertion XML, leading to mismatched timestamp comparisons and assertion validation failures.
resolution: Short-term workaround: Customer updated nginx rewrite to preserve fractional seconds (use $msec or $time_iso8601 with millisecond support) — eliminated failures. Long-term fix: ENG patch to idp-proxy to (1) prefer the assertion's Conditions timestamp when present, (2) robustly parse ISO-8601 with optional fractional seconds for any header fallback, and (3) add unit tests. Patch merged to main and scheduled for next patch release. Added integration test in ci/infra to replay SAML assertions with millisecond precision through ingress.
postmortem_followup: ENG: backport idp-proxy fix to v1.12.x (priority P1). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1427
Support: add KB article for customers on preserving fractional-second timestamps in header rewrites and recommended nginx variables to use.
SRE: add an alert when token-exchange assertion validation failure rate > 5% for 10m to detect regressions early.
Security: confirm signature verification invariants unchanged by parsing change (security review completed by Tomás).
